# Taskmesh

> Taskmesh is a governed AI workflow orchestration platform for building, approving, running, and monitoring business workflows that combine agents, tools, APIs, deterministic logic, secure Python computation, and human decisions.

Canonical site: https://taskme.sh/

## Core product

- Visual workflow composition with agents, tools, decisions, switches, loops, delays, merges, and human tasks.
- Draft validation and immutable published workflow versions.
- Organization-scoped users, workflows, tools, credentials, permissions, and runs.
- Human approval checkpoints before sensitive actions.
- Node-level workflow-run history and audit context.
- Custom API operations through published external APIs.
- JSON extraction and transformation tools.
- Sandboxed Python computation without network or credential access.

## Important pages

- [Homepage](https://taskme.sh/): Product overview and core positioning.

- [Security](https://taskme.sh/security.html): Access boundaries, approvals, auditability, integrations, and Python isolation.
- [Integrations](https://taskme.sh/integrations.html): API operations, connections, JSON tools, and Python computation.
- [Use cases](https://taskme.sh/use-cases.html): Finance reconciliation, approval-driven actions, data operations, and internal assistants.
- [Blog](https://taskme.sh/blog/): Practical guidance for designing governed, inspectable AI workflows.

## Selected articles

- [Governed bank reconciliation](https://taskme.sh/blog/2026/governed-bank-reconciliation.html): A reference architecture for parallel accounting data retrieval, AI-assisted investigation, controlled record creation, and run evidence.
- [Human approval in AI workflows](https://taskme.sh/blog/2026/human-approval-ai-workflows.html): Guidance for placing approval at meaningful decision boundaries and giving reviewers the context they need.
- [Agents versus deterministic tools](https://taskme.sh/blog/2026/agents-vs-deterministic-tools.html): A framework for deciding which workflow steps need model reasoning and which should use code, rules, or APIs.

## Terminology

- Taskmesh: The product and platform name.
- Workflow: A versioned graph of agents, tools, logic, and human tasks.
- Human task: A workflow step that pauses execution for an authorized person’s decision.
- Published version: An immutable workflow definition selected for controlled execution.
- Tool: An approved operation a workflow can invoke, such as an API call or data transformation.

## Integration policy

Taskmesh interacts with external business platforms through their published APIs. Taskmesh workflows, scripts, and background jobs do not connect directly to an external platform’s database.
